result.topic_en: A worked numerical example, done with logarithms, for a set of six coefficients A, B, C, a, b, c. A value G is tested through the differences G−A, G−B and G−C, apparently a root of the characteristic (principal-axis) equation of a ternary quadratic form, and two angles are derived.

methods.what: Logarithmic computation: the coefficients a, b, c are entered as common logarithms, with 'n' marking a negative value, and combined by addition.
A trial root G of a cubic (apparently the characteristic equation of a ternary quadratic form) is checked by the logarithms of the differences G−A, G−B and G−C together with a, b, c.
Angles in degrees, minutes and seconds are derived from the logarithmic quantities, apparently the orientation of the principal axes.
